tagline: Across Natural Bridge, and up the Tye River Turnpike.
intro: This byway comes in two short pieces. US 11 runs south out of Lexington to Natural Bridge and goes over the top of it.

To the northeast, Route 56 leaves US 11 at Steeles Tavern, 1,683 feet up and a short way from the McCormick farm, as the Tye River Turnpike. It enters the George Washington National Forest, passes under the railroad at Vesuvius and winds up the Blue Ridge beside Little Marys Creek to meet the Parkway at Tye River Gap.

moments.title: Lexington
moments.text: Named in 1778 for the Massachusetts town of the Revolution's first shot, the second of many American places to borrow the name.

moments.title: Natural Bridge
moments.text: US 11 rides across the top of a 215-foot limestone arch over Cedar Creek, though the fences along it hide nearly everything but the pavement.

moments.title: Cyrus McCormick Farm
moments.text: At Walnut Grove, in the farm's blacksmith shop, Cyrus McCormick worked out the mechanical reaper that led in time to the combine harvester.
